name: Lumbini & the Buddha's Nepal
tagline: The Buddha's birthplace and the Kapilavastu sites
meta_description: Lumbini tours: Maya Devi Temple, Tilaurakot, Ramagrama and Devdaha, plus Tansen and the Sonauli border. Buddhist circuit prices, seasons, fees and routes.
summary: Lumbini, 22 km from the Sonauli border and a 35-minute flight from Kathmandu to Bhairahawa, is the birthplace of the Buddha. Two nights cover the Maya Devi Temple and the monastic zone; four or five add Tilaurakot, Kudan, Niglihawa, Ramagrama and Devdaha. Tansen, at 1,350 m, adds hill-town heritage. Best months: October–March.
intro: Lumbini lies in the flat western Terai of Rupandehi district, about 300 km south-west of Kathmandu and only a short drive from the Indian border. Here, according to Buddhist tradition, Queen Maya Devi gave birth to Siddhartha Gautama in a sal grove around the 6th century BCE. Emperor Ashoka marked the spot with an inscribed pillar about 249 BCE, and today the Maya Devi Temple shelters the marker stone above the excavated foundations. UNESCO listed Lumbini as a World Heritage Site in 1997.

Around the Sacred Garden spreads the master-plan area designed by Kenzo Tange, about 4.8 km long, with a central canal, the Eternal Peace Flame and two monastic zones where Buddhist nations have built temples in their own styles: Thai, Myanmar, Chinese, Korean, German, Vietnamese and many more. Monks chant at dawn, sarus cranes feed in the wetlands to the north, and the World Peace Pagoda catches the last light. Two nights are enough for Lumbini itself.

The wider region holds the rest of the Buddha's early life. Tilaurakot, 27 km west, is identified with Kapilavastu, the Shakya capital where Siddhartha grew up. Kudan, Gotihawa and Niglihawa preserve Ashoka pillars and stupas. Ramagrama keeps a relic stupa believed never to have been opened, and Devdaha, near Butwal, was the home of Maya Devi's Koliya clan. North of the plains, Tansen at 1,350 m is a Newar hill town known for dhaka weaving and the Rani Mahal palace on the Kali Gandaki.

For Indian travellers, Lumbini is the easiest part of Nepal to reach: the Sonauli–Belahiya border is about three hours from Gorakhpur, and no visa is needed with a passport or voter ID. Many pilgrims join it with Kushinagar, Sarnath and Bodh Gaya on a cross-border Buddhist circuit, or continue north to Pokhara and Kathmandu. Our packages range from 2-night Lumbini pilgrimages to 9-night tours from Varanasi, priced in INR and USD.

highlights.title: Maya Devi Temple and the marker stone
highlights.text: Inside the white Maya Devi Temple, a walkway leads over excavated brick foundations to the marker stone said to fix the exact place of the Buddha's birth. Outside are the Ashoka pillar of about 249 BCE, the Puskarini pond where Maya Devi is said to have bathed, and a bodhi tree hung with prayer flags.

highlights.title: Monasteries of many nations
highlights.text: The master-plan area has two monastic zones: Mahayana and Vajrayana temples to the west, Theravada to the east. A 12–15 km cycle loop takes in the Royal Thai Monastery, the Myanmar Golden Temple, China's Zhong Hua Temple and the German Lotus Stupa, ending at the World Peace Pagoda.

highlights.title: Tilaurakot, the Shakya capital
highlights.text: Tilaurakot, 27 km west of Lumbini, is the walled city identified with Kapilavastu, where Siddhartha lived as a prince until he left at 29. Brick foundations, the moat and the eastern gate of his departure lie in quiet mango and sal groves, with the Kapilvastu Museum nearby.

highlights.title: Ashoka pillars and an unopened stupa
highlights.text: At Niglihawa and Gotihawa, broken pillars raised by Emperor Ashoka mark sites of earlier Buddhas, and Niglihawa's inscription contains the earliest known written use of the word stupa. East of Lumbini, the grassy mound of Ramagrama is believed to be the only original relic stupa never opened.

highlights.title: Tansen and Rani Mahal
highlights.text: Tansen, a Newar hill town at 1,350 m, is a two-hour drive north of Butwal. Its steep lanes hold temples and dhaka weaving workshops, Srinagar hill gives Himalayan views on clear mornings, and a 13 km road or hike leads down to Rani Mahal, an 1893 palace on the Kali Gandaki.

highlights.title: Buddha Jayanti in Lumbini
highlights.text: On the full moon of Baisakh, in late April or May, Lumbini marks the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death with processions, chanting by monks from many countries and butter lamps around the Maya Devi Temple. Tens of thousands attend despite heat near 40 °C, so rooms must be booked months ahead.

getting_there: Gautam Buddha International Airport at Bhairahawa is about 20 km from Lumbini, with several daily domestic flights from Kathmandu taking about 35 minutes. International services there have been limited and seasonal, so check current status before you travel. By road, Kathmandu to Lumbini is about 300 km and 8–10 hours via Mugling, Narayangarh and Butwal; Pokhara is about 210 km and 7–8 hours via the Siddhartha Highway; Chitwan is about 165 km and 4.5–5 hours. From India, most travellers cross at Sonauli–Belahiya, about 100 km and three hours from Gorakhpur, then drive 22–30 km to Lumbini. Kushinagar is about 175 km away and Varanasi about 330 km. Travellers coming from Bihar can also cross at Raxaul–Birgunj and drive about 270 km west via Narayangarh.
permits: No permits are needed to tour Lumbini and the Buddhist sites. The Lumbini Development Trust charges a conservation fee for the Maya Devi Temple area; as we understand it, the rates rose in 2026 to about NPR 700 for SAARC and Myanmar nationals, including Indians, and NPR 1,000 for other foreigners, with monks and nuns exempt. Tilaurakot, the Kapilvastu Museum and Rani Mahal charge small separate fees. Indians cross the border with a passport or voter ID; other nationalities buy a Nepal visa on arrival at Belahiya. Check current status before you travel.

months.weather: Lumbini 8 to 21 °C, dry, dense fog until mid-morning
months.summary: January is cold for the Terai, with thick fog that often blankets Lumbini until 10 or 11 am and can delay morning flights into Bhairahawa. Afternoons are mild and sunny, ideal for the monastic zone and the Kapilavastu sites. Pilgrim groups from Sri Lanka, Thailand and Myanmar are common. Tansen, at 1,350 m, often sits above the fog with clear Himalayan views from Srinagar hill, though nights there fall to about 6 °C.
months.tip: Plan outlying sites for the afternoon and book a late-morning flight to Bhairahawa to avoid fog delays.

months.summary: February is one of the best months in Lumbini. Fog thins out, days are warm and dry, and the light is clear for photographs of the Maya Devi Temple and the monasteries. It is a comfortable time for a full circuit of Tilaurakot, Kudan, Gotihawa and Niglihawa, with sarus cranes still feeding in the wetlands. Mustard fields flower yellow around the Kapilavastu sites, and Tansen is pleasant for walking.
months.tip: Combine the Kapilavastu sites in one long day and finish with sunset at the World Peace Pagoda.

months.summary: March is warm and dry, a good month for the eastern sites of Ramagrama and Devdaha, which need longer drives. Mornings are fresh and afternoons warm enough to plan a midday rest. Holi brings colour to Bhairahawa and Butwal, so allow for closed shops and boisterous streets on the day. Tansen's rhododendrons begin to flower on the higher ridges, and Rani Mahal makes a fine half-day hike.
months.tip: Leave Lumbini by 7:30 am for Ramagrama and Devdaha to finish before the afternoon heat.

months.summary: April turns hot, with afternoons near 37 °C and hazy skies. Pilgrim numbers fall, except when Buddha Jayanti arrives on the Baisakh full moon in late April. Plan site visits for dawn and late afternoon and rest in air-conditioned rooms at midday. Tansen, about 10 °C cooler than the plains, is a good escape for a night or two, with clear evenings and the start of the pre-monsoon breezes.
months.tip: Visit the Sacred Garden at opening time, around 6 am, when the stone paths are still cool underfoot.

months.weather: Lumbini 24 to 38 °C, up to 42 °C, hot with pre-monsoon storms
months.summary: May is the hottest month, with highs that can reach 42 °C. The reason to come is Buddha Jayanti, which in many years falls on the May full moon and brings tens of thousands of pilgrims, monks' processions and butter lamps to the Maya Devi Temple. Book rooms months ahead and keep outings to early mornings. Outside the festival, Tansen and its cooler hills are the more comfortable base.
months.tip: Carry a hat, an umbrella for shade and at least 2 litres of water during Buddha Jayanti.

months.weather: Lumbini 26 to 36 °C, very humid, monsoon from mid-month
months.summary: June is hot and sticky until the monsoon arrives around mid-month. Rain then cools the air slightly but raises humidity, and site paths at Tilaurakot and Kudan turn muddy. Mosquitoes increase, so carry repellent. Lumbini's Sacred Garden and monasteries stay open and quiet, and short visits by air remain practical. Rice planting begins across the Terai, and the green fields are good for photographs between showers.
months.tip: Keep June trips short and based in Lumbini, with a car on standby for showers.

months.weather: Lumbini 26 to 33 °C, heavy monsoon rain, humid
months.summary: July is the wettest month, with heavy downpours, waterlogged fields and slow roads, especially on the Siddhartha Highway to Tansen and Pokhara, where landslides are common. Lumbini itself stays open and almost empty, and the monasteries are peaceful for meditation, with some centres running monsoon retreats. Outlying sites can be hard to reach after heavy rain. For a full circuit, wait until October.
months.tip: Fly to Bhairahawa rather than drive in July, and check current status before you travel.

months.weather: Lumbini 26 to 33 °C, monsoon rain; Tansen 19 to 27 °C
months.summary: August remains wet and humid on the plains, but the hills are cooler and green. Tansen celebrates Bhagwati Jatra, its biggest festival, on the day after Krishna Janmashtami, when the goddess's chariot is pulled through the old town in memory of the 1815 battle. Roads to Tansen can be slow after rain. Lumbini is quiet, with good conditions for meditation and few visitors at the Maya Devi Temple.
months.tip: Stay in Tansen the night before Bhagwati Jatra to see the chariot leave in the morning.

months.summary: The monsoon fades through September and the Terai turns green and gold as rice ripens. Showers become shorter, roads improve and pilgrim groups begin to return late in the month. Humidity stays high, so plan early starts. In some years Bhagwati Jatra in Tansen falls in early September. Tilaurakot and Niglihawa are lush and quiet, and late September is a sensible shoulder month for a short Lumbini trip.
months.tip: Use mosquito repellent at dawn and dusk; the wetlands around Lumbini are still full of water.

months.weather: Lumbini 20 to 31 °C, dry and clear after the monsoon
months.summary: October opens the main pilgrim season. Skies are clear, the air is fresh after the rains and the drives to Ramagrama and Devdaha are easy. Monastery groups from across Asia arrive, and Dashain and Tihar bring Nepali visitors and holidays to Butwal and Bhairahawa. Tansen has its clearest Himalayan views of the year from Srinagar hill. Book hotels early, especially around Diwali.
months.tip: Reserve Lumbini hotels four to six weeks ahead for October; monastery groups fill rooms quickly.

months.weather: Lumbini 14 to 28 °C, dry, sunny, cool mornings
months.summary: November is the most comfortable month for the full Buddhist circuit, with sunny days in the mid-20s and cool mornings. Sarus cranes return to the wetlands around Lumbini, and the light at Tilaurakot and Kudan is soft in the late afternoon. Many cross-border tours from Kushinagar and Sarnath come through Sonauli now. Chhath, after Diwali, brings sunrise offerings at ponds and rivers around Bhairahawa.
months.tip: Allow an extra hour at the Sonauli border during November, when pilgrim traffic is heaviest.

months.weather: Lumbini 9 to 23 °C, dry, foggy mornings from mid-month
months.summary: December is cool and dry, with fog building in the second half of the month. Days are pleasant for walking and cycling around the monastic zone, and the Kapilavastu sites are quiet. Late December brings winter-holiday groups from India and abroad. Tansen is cold at night, around 7 °C, but its mornings are often clear above the plains' fog, and the Rani Mahal hike is comfortable.
months.tip: Pack warm socks: shoes come off at the Maya Devi Temple and the stone floors are cold in winter.

faqs.q: How many days are needed for Lumbini?
faqs.a: Two nights is enough for Lumbini itself: the Sacred Garden and Maya Devi Temple at dawn, the monastic zones and the World Peace Pagoda. Add one night for Tilaurakot, Kudan and Niglihawa, and another for Ramagrama and Devdaha. With Tansen and Rani Mahal, plan five or six nights in the region.

faqs.q: How do I reach Lumbini from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Fly from Kathmandu to Bhairahawa in about 35 minutes and drive about 20 km, around 40 minutes, to Lumbini. By road it is about 300 km and 8–10 hours via Mugling, Narayangarh and Butwal, by private car or tourist bus. Many travellers break the drive with two nights in Chitwan.

faqs.q: How far is Lumbini from the Indian border?
faqs.a: Lumbini is about 22–30 km from the Sonauli–Belahiya border, around 45 minutes by car. Gorakhpur, the nearest major railway junction, is about 100 km and three hours from the border, Kushinagar about 175 km from Lumbini and Varanasi about 330 km. Indian vehicles need a customs permit at the border.

faqs.q: What is the Lumbini Maya Devi Temple entry fee?
faqs.a: As we understand it, the Lumbini Development Trust raised its conservation fee in 2026 to about NPR 700 for SAARC and Myanmar nationals, including Indians, and NPR 1,000 for other foreigners. Monks, nuns and local residents are exempt. Tickets are sold at the gate and online. Fees change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Lumbini?
faqs.a: October to March, with February, March, October and November ideal: dry days of 18–30 °C. December and January are cool with dense morning fog. April to June is very hot, up to 42 °C, though Buddha Jayanti in late April or May draws huge crowds. The June to September monsoon is humid and wet.

faqs.q: Do Indians need a passport or visa for Lumbini?
faqs.a: Indian citizens need no visa for Nepal. A valid passport or voter ID card is enough to cross at Sonauli or fly into Nepal; Aadhaar and PAN cards are not accepted. Children can usually travel with a birth certificate or school ID with parents. Rules can change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When is Buddha Jayanti in Lumbini?
faqs.a: Buddha Jayanti falls on the full moon of the Nepali month of Baisakh, usually in late April or May. Lumbini holds processions, chanting by monks from many countries and butter-lamp offerings at the Maya Devi Temple. Book rooms several months ahead, expect temperatures near 40 °C and confirm the date for your year before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I combine Lumbini with Pokhara and Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Yes, and many Indian families do. A common loop is Sonauli to Lumbini, then 210 km and 7–8 hours to Pokhara via the Siddhartha Highway with a stop in Tansen, then on to Kathmandu, about 7 nights in total. Adding Chitwan between Lumbini and Kathmandu makes a 9–10 night tour.

faqs.q: Is Tansen worth visiting from Lumbini?
faqs.a: Yes, for one or two nights. Tansen sits at 1,350 m, about 90 km and 2.5–3 hours north of Lumbini, and is cooler than the plains. Its Newar old town, dhaka weaving workshops, sunrise views from Srinagar hill and the Rani Mahal palace on the Kali Gandaki make a good contrast with the pilgrimage sites.
